paragraphs: Here's what this whole passage is telling you, friend: God sees what was done to His people, and He answers. Jerusalem lays out her hurt, and she doesn't hold back (Jeremiah 51:34-35). Then the LORD says, "Behold, I will plead your case and take vengeance on your behalf" (Jeremiah 51:36). Nobody in that moment had to settle the score alone.

Now look at how big Babylon was. It was "the praise of all the earth," and it had a wall, a king and a god named Bel (Jeremiah 51:41, 44). Yet the LORD says "the LORD's intentions against Babylon stand" (Jeremiah 51:29), and I'll tell you, nothing built by people can stand against that. Every wall, every crown and every idol has an expiration date, and only the LORD's word keeps going.

So why does this matter to you, baker? When life feels unfair and you're tempted to carry every wrong yourself, this passage hands you a lighter load. You can bring it to God honestly, the way Jerusalem did, and trust Him to be the one who pleads your case. And keep your oven warm, because Jeremiah's message against Babylon isn't finished yet.
